literal: Easy thinking, house he-who-trespasses will-attain always without-perishing will-stand disgrace.
translation: He who trespasses into another's house thinking it is easy will attain a disgrace that stands forever without fading.
modern: இது எளிது என்று நினைத்து அடுத்தவர் வீட்டிற்குள் எல்லை மீறிச் செல்பவன், எக்காலத்திலும் அழியாமல் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் பழியை அடைவான்.
explanation: The couplet warns against the temptation of illicit affairs by highlighting the permanent damage to one's reputation. The word 'il' has multiple meanings including 'not', but here it means 'house', specifically referring to trespassing into a neighbor's home. A person might think such a transgression is easy to commit and hide. However, the resulting disgrace will never perish and will stand against him forever.
